# GMAA, Governed Multi-Agent Architecture

> GMAA is an architectural framework for coding systems with multiple agents. It runs on Claude Code and Grok Build and authorizes the complete set of pending changes, not only each change alone. Approval of each change stays in place. GMAA adds one accountable human, in a governed seat independent of every agent, who ratifies the whole set against the rules the system must keep before anything commits. The unit of authorization is the set.

Key facts:
- Author and operator: Israel Heskiel
- Specification: Governed Multi-Agent Architecture, current version v1.6.9 (2026-11-06), licensed CC BY 4.0, cite by version
- Engine: reference implementations, gmaa-engine for Claude Code and gmaa-engine-grok for Grok Build, with source available under Apache 2.0 with the Commons Clause (free to use, modify, and redistribute, but not to be sold or offered as a paid or hosted service)
- Repository: https://github.com/gmaa-ai/gmaa
- The claim: systems of multiple agents fail by authorizing at the wrong unit. Individually approved changes can be jointly incoherent, and the complete pending set must be ratified before commit
- Not claimed: completeness by assertion. Whether an implementation catches every joint incoherence is answered by adversarial testing, not asserted

## Pages

- [Home](https://gmaa.ai/): what GMAA is, how it works, key capabilities, FAQ
- [Thesis](https://gmaa.ai/thesis.html): The Coherence Boundary, the argument for the set as the unit of authorization and why the governed seat cannot be filled by an agent
- [Architecture](https://gmaa.ai/canon.html): the full v1.6.9 specification, coherence boundaries, the discipline of a single writer, the governed seat, ratification flow, instantiation checklist
- [How it works](https://gmaa.ai/how-it-works.html): the operating loop in practice
- [Use cases](https://gmaa.ai/applications.html): where set-level authorization applies
- [Engine map](https://gmaa.ai/engine-map.html): how the engine implements the specification, the engine's own map (ENGINE-MAP.md in v2.7.2) of every file in the release, grouped into ten functional areas with the execution wiring
- [Versions](https://gmaa.ai/versions.html): release history, current artifacts, download verification, and the current engine version with its canon pin. Two engine lines, one specification, versioned separately. The Claude line is at gmaa-engine v2.7.2 with canon pin v1.6.9: a decision kit beside the engine zip, genesis in one command, and every writing seat signing its commits and relays with its own key. Hotfix HF1 for v2.7.2, at github.com/gmaa-ai/gmaa/tree/main/hotfix/v2.7.2-hf1, fixes false permission prompts and a restart that waited on a prompt, and a project that applies it cites v2.7.2-hf1. The Grok line, at github.com/gmaa-ai/gmaa/tree/main/grok, is at gmaa-engine-grok v2.5.7 with canon pin v1.6.1, with a plugin route for Grok Build and a Grok Bot route for the chat architect. Advisory (Claude line): projects adopted on v2.7 take v2.7.2 as an engine update, and v2.5.7 slot fills do not carry over to the v2.7 line.
- [Operator's guide](https://gmaa.ai/operator-guide.html): running the framework as the accountable operator
- [Field evidence](https://gmaa.ai/field-evidence.html): receipted incidents behind the architecture's failure classes
- [Field notes: The Second Empty Chair](https://gmaa.ai/second-empty-chair.html): the context window as an ungoverned coherence boundary, why session degradation is an authorization problem and not only a capacity problem, and what a governed retention regime looks like
- [Seven Models Read the Second Empty Chair](https://gmaa.ai/sevenmodels.html): reactions from seven frontier models to governing the context window with set-level authorization, quoted from real sessions. Six of seven misread the seat as a person
- [Governed Context](https://gmaa.ai/governed-context.html): the full design for governing the AI context window, with ratified sets at entry, residency computed from declared roots, and a record layer at exit. It has two coherence boundaries, the window and the record, each with one writer and the commit gate between them. It is design draft r9, not benchmarked
- [Governed Context, the short version](https://gmaa.ai/gc-short.html): the same design in about 1,600 words, covering the claim, the three edges, what it does not promise, and the open problems. It is the entry point for readers new to the argument, and it includes where the accountable seat sits when the window belongs to the serving stack
- [Field notes](https://gmaa.ai/field-notes.html): index of the field notes

## Optional
